notes:
K8Secret 0.6.20 — it opens on your whole cluster.

The app used to start in the namespace called default. On most clusters that is the one namespace with nothing in it, so the first thing you saw was an empty app beside a cluster that was working perfectly well — and the setting responsible sat in the titlebar corner, which is where you were least likely to look. When default did not exist it fell back to whichever namespace the API server listed first, so two people on the same cluster could land somewhere different.

It now opens on every namespace. If your kubeconfig context names a namespace, that still wins — that is your own kubectl setting, and the one case where a single namespace is a decision rather than a guess.

Browsing every namespace is also much cheaper. It used to be one request per namespace, per list, and the sidebar asks for seven lists at once — so a large cluster opened with hundreds of requests. K8Secret now asks the API server for the whole cluster in a single request per list, which is what makes this a sensible default rather than an expensive one.
